one_liner: Header-only SSE library for 3D projective geometric algebra; its llvm-mca listings show about half GLM's estimated cycles for quaternion and dual-quaternion work.
what_it_does: Klein implements 3D projective geometric algebra P(R*_{3,0,1}) with fixed types for points, directions, lines, ideal lines, planes, rotors (quaternions), translators and motors (dual quaternions). Rigid transforms are applied by calling a rotor or motor on an entity (m(p)), composed with operator*, intersected and joined with ^ and &, and converted to column-major 3x4 or 4x4 matrices for shaders. It replaces a quaternion, dual-quaternion and matrix stack such as GLM; it is not a drop-in replacement, because the types, operators and memory layout are its own.
how_it_is_fast: Klein supports only one algebra in one dimension, so every product was worked out by hand. The non-zero terms of each geometric product and sandwich (conjugation) are packed into blocks of four floats, one __m128 register each, and computed with shufps, mulps and addps. A rotor uses one register and a motor uses two. Motor-point application (sw312) evaluates m p ~m directly, without building a matrix. Normalization and inversion use rcpps and rsqrtps with one Newton-Raphson step instead of division and sqrt. Array overloads such as motor::operator()(point* in, point* out, size_t count) reuse the motor-derived terms across a packed batch.
when_to_use: Skinning, animation or kinematic-chain code on x86 that composes many rigid transforms and applies them to points, using float32 motors (8 floats) in place of 4x4 matrices.

Geometry code that needs points, lines and planes in one system: intersecting planes into lines, joining points into lines and planes, projecting, and measuring distances and angles without special-case formulas.
Interpolating rigid-body motion with the motor logarithm and line exponentiation that the library provides.
Transforming large packed arrays of points, planes or lines by one motor with the array call operator.
Targets guaranteed to have SSE3, or SSE4.1 for the dpps path via the klein_sse42 target, where single precision is enough.
when_not_to_use: Pure quaternion composition: RTM's quat_mul is at parity in the project's own listing (824 vs 821 estimated cycles, block reciprocal throughput 7.0 vs 8.0), and RTM is maintained.
ARM, Apple Silicon or WebAssembly: these work only through the optional SIMDe shim (KLEIN_USE_SIMDE), none of the published analysis covers them, and Emscripten issue #28 is open.
Double precision, general-dimension algebras or a general multivector type: every type is float32 in __m128 registers, limited to the entity list in the docs.

Projects that need a maintained dependency: the repo was archived on 2024-08-02, and issue #30 (line*line geometric product gpLL builds a motor around the wrong axis because e23 and e12 are swapped) was filed a week earlier with a patch and never merged.
Code that needs exactly normalized results: normalize(), invert() and point::normalize() use rcpps or rsqrtps plus one Newton step (about 22 bits per the source comments).

integration.dependencies: none for the core headers (copy public/ and include <klein/klein.hpp>); SIMDe only for the optional non-x86 shim
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (a C++11 fallback .inl replaces the C++17 'if constexpr' paths; the klein_sse42 target sets C++17); README tests GCC 9.2.1, Clang 9.0.1, Visual Studio 2019 and Xcode 11.3; needs -msse3, or -msse4.1 with KLEIN_SSE_4_1
integration.platforms: x86/x86-64 with SSE3 (SSE4.1 optional); other architectures only through the SIMDe shim, untested in the published analysis
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the headers read hold only __m128 value members and no shared mutable state

gotchas: Harness flaw in the GLM motor row of docs/perf.md (5435 vs 1831 cycles). The routine is glm::mat3x4_cast(a) * b with b a glm::vec4. GLM 0.9.9.7 has no mat3x4 * vec4 operator, and GLM_EXPLICIT is empty unless GLM_FORCE_EXPLICIT_CTOR is set, so b silently converts to a vec3. Because mat3x4_cast stores the rows of [R|t] as the matrix's columns, the line computes R^T p with no translation and puts t.p in w. That is not the rigid transform Klein computes; the correct call is b * mat3x4_cast(a). The listing confirms it: only 0, 4 and 8(%rsi) of the point are loaded. The GLM routine also normalizes the dual quaternion on every call (x.real / length2(x.real), 4 divss with 11-cycle latency), which Klein's m(p) skips because it assumes a normalized motor. So the about 3x gap compares a normalize-and-build-matrix routine that computes a different result against a direct sandwich.

The verifier's caveat that GLM ran without its SIMD path matters less than it sounds for rotor composition. In GLM 0.9.9.7 the SIMD compute_quat_mul in detail/type_quat_simd.inl is commented out, so quat*quat is scalar even with GLM_FORCE_INTRINSICS. The scalar listing (5700 instructions per 100 iterations) is representative of that GLM version. Five of its 57 instructions are a stack round-trip from returning a 16-byte struct in two XMM registers under the SysV ABI.

Types are 16-byte-aligned __m128 wrappers. point::store() uses the aligned _mm_store_ps on a plain float* while load() is unaligned. The memory layout is (w, x, y, z) with the homogeneous coordinate first, not GLM's (x, y, z, w). Containers of Klein types before C++17 need aligned allocation.

CMake add_subdirectory always FetchContent-populates SIMDe v0.7.2 from GitHub at configure time, even with KLEIN_ENABLE_SIMDE off; copying public/ avoids this. The standalone perf build clones RTM over an SSH URL (git@github.com) at origin/master, and on non-Windows it takes any installed GLM through find_package before the pinned 0.9.9.7, so a rebuild of the analysis may use different baselines.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Klein over xsimd when you want ready-made rotor, motor, point, line and plane operations on SSE rather than portable SIMD primitives for writing your own kernels. No other catalogued sibling covers rigid-body transforms. Pick xsimd, or a general tensor library such as Axiom, for wider-than-128-bit SIMD, ARM or double precision.
verified_claims_summary: No run time was measured. docs/perf.md gives llvm-mca static estimates (Intel Skylake scheduling model, 100 iterations, dispatch width 6) for code regions marked with mc_ruler; the compiler is clang through mc_ruler, version unstated. Rotor composition: Klein 821 estimated cycles vs scalar GLM 0.9.9.7 quat*quat at 1522 (1.85x, derived from page data) and RTM at 824 (parity). Motor-point application: Klein 1831 vs 5435 (2.97x, derived from page data), but the GLM routine normalizes, builds a 3x4 matrix and applies its transpose without translation. perf/rtm_perf.cpp has an RTM qvv point-transform routine whose result is not published.
status_note: Archived since 2024-08-02 (the author calls it temporary) with line-product bug #30 unfixed. MIT-licensed, header-only and dependency-free, so it is small enough to vendor and patch for SSE x86 targets.
